newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-MARTIN ROUTS LEADERS WITH CAREER-BEST 8-32.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MARTIN ROUTS LEADERS WITH CAREER-BEST 8-32.

text.p: Lancashire fast-medium bowler Peter Martin captured a career-best eight for 32 to rout English county championship leaders Middlesex on Wednesday.
Martin, making the most of a damp pitch at Uxbridge, had a spell of five for eight in seven overs to reduce Middlesex to 42 for seven at one stage.
Middlesex were bowled out for 118 and Lancashire consolidated by making 124 without loss at the close of the first day of the four-day match.
An eighth wicket stand of 54 between Owais Shah and Jamie Hewitt gave the leaders a degree of respectability before Martin polished off the innings after lunch by taking the last three wickets.
Martin beat his previous best of seven for 50 against Nottinghamshire last season.
By the time Lancashire's first innings started the pitch had dried out, allowing opener Nathan Wood to reach his maiden first-class half-century in 113 deliveries. He was 67 not out at the close.
Fourth-placed Kent, only nine points behind Middlesex with a game in hand, were rescued by half-centuries from Nigel Llong and Zimbabwe leg-spinner Paul Strang against Northamptonshire at Maidstone.

Kent were lifted from 149 for six to 306 all out as Llong, who reached his 50 off 97 balls with eight fours, hit 57 and Strang, who completed a fine half-century off 91 balls with seven fours, made 55.
There was a late flourish from Ben Phillips, until he was bowled for 47 by Pakistan fellow paceman Mohammad Akram, who took four for 56.
Second-placed Essex, two points behind Middlesex, battled to 280 all out against Somerset at Chelmsford after a last wicket stand of 66.
Fast bowler Ashley Cowan, who hit an unbeaten 46, and former England off-spinner Peter Such lifted their side from 214 for nine.
Left-arm paceman Mark Ilott then jolted Somerset by firing out Peter Bowler and Simon Ecclestone without a run on the board. The visitors were 42 for two at the close.
Yorkshire captain David Byas hit a gritty, unbeaten 66 to hold his side's innings together on a rain-affected first day against champions Leicestershire.
Only 42 overs were possible at Leicester in which Yorkshire struggled to 149 for five, Byas making his runs off 75 balls and hitting 12 fours to steer the side from 86 for four.
